correctness.rationale: PASS: Multiplicativity and β(p^a)=(p^{a+1}+(-1)^a)/(p+1) give β≥φ. For odd prime powers a≥2 and for two odd prime supports, 1<(n−1)/β(n)<2; for powers of 2 only n=4 is an exception. For n=2^a p^b, parity of β(p^b) forces b even; a=1 forces quotient 2 and absurd 2p^b=p+3, while a≥2 and p≥5 or p=3 with a even yield quotient below 2. Final p=3, odd a≥3 forces integer quotient 2 and 3^{b+1}−2^{a+1}=5, contradicted mod 8 since b even. The prime case β(p)=p−1 holds. Independently recomputed Liouville-convolution β(n) for n≤5000 and checked every ω(n)≤2 divisibility hit is prime or four. Finite checks do not prove all exponents.
